chapter: Band personalities, Duke's last years and the office
title: Marijuana scare crossing into Canada
summary: A cigarette stub was found by Carney; Duke vouched for him at the 600 Club and Tizol had to show a birth certificate.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: We were talking about crossing borders with the band, and you mentioned an incident that

happened once going in to Canada on the train. Whereabouts in Canada was it? Oh, I don't know what place it was -- Montreal, or Toronto; I guess it was one of those places, and they stopped the train one place, and we didn't know what was happening, and all of a sudden a bunch of men came in to our private car. We started telling them that this was a private car, and to go someplace else.

So they didn't say nothing. So they stopped the car and they started telling people to sit down, and you sit down, and you and you -- they were telling all the boys in the band to sit down, and so we figured, I guess they were detectives looking for dope or something.

So they started looking in suitcases and this and the other and so forth, and they passed by and happened to see where Carney was sitting down, a little piece of cigarette and they find out it was marijuana, so the boys in the band figured that maybe Toby smoked it and threw the butt away, you know?
Because Harry did not use it, right?

So they took him to headquarters, and one of the principals in the 600 Club, Duke went over there and explained that he was a principal man in the band and was needed for the concert, or the dance or whatever it was, and that he didn't use any dope. That, after all, we had a private car with people passing through all the time -- anybody
could have thrown it there. So they took his story and let him go.
Good. The 600 Club was where you were working.
Huh?
The 600 Club was the place you were working in the Canadian city.
Yeah. The 600 Club.
So they dropped all the charges against Harry.
Yeah.
Good.
Oh, they were hard on American people coming in to Canada then, because they were bringing a lot of dope in and everything, so I guess they had to do it.
And they were hard on Juan. He had to take his birth certificate and everything with him.

Oh, sure, I had to. They wouldn't believe you -- I had to show my birth certificate; I used to tell them I was a Puerto Rican, and they said, 'What do you mean? Anybody can say they are Puerto Rican. You got to show me something to back it up.'
I think the only time I ever crossed the border with a band was going to Vancouver, and I remember there was no problem at all, when we went in, nobody searched

anything, and the Canadians were very cordial to the band bus, but when we came back out of Canada, going to Seattle, the Americans searched everything. I remember Al Kelley telling everybody in the bus before we got to the border, he said, 'if anybody has anything, get rid of it quick, because they're not going to be easy; they're not going to overlook anything.'

Oh, what's his name? Duke and Sid, they used to make a speech everytime we went to Canada; they used to say, 'Now be careful; get rid of everything you have in your pockets before you get on the train to Canada, because they will search everything.'
